title: Ordinary geometric open extension of semilinear systems
statement: Let W be a scheme, V an open object of its pro-etale site, and B a strict tower of commutative ring sheaves. Fix any normalized open coefficient datum A [def-pur-sequence-site-open-data]. Then there exists an ordinary geometric sequence open datum O, with O.coefficients=A, satisfying the actual ordinary transition equation for every pair n≤m. All geometric localization, sectionwise restriction, exact adjunction, level comparison and evaluated unit/counit fields are conclusions. No scalar-preservation or derived assertion is part of this statement.

source.place: Tags 04GZ, 0791, 04IE, 03DI and 03DJ: original proof steps 1, 2, 5 and 6.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C=W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $I=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and let $\mathcal T_W$ be the sequence site in [lem-pur-sequence-site-completion-projection]. Put $H=h_V$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], $H(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_W(U,V)$ has at most one element and $\mathcal C/H=\mathcal C/V$ identifies with $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$, including coverings. By [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], the constant diagram $\Delta H$ is a sheaf on $\mathcal T_W$. Its element site has objects $(U,n,s:U\to V)$; an arrow consists of $a:U'\to U$ and $k\le n$ with $s'=sa$. Its generating covers are precisely the fixed-index covers over $V$. Thus this element site is $(\mathcal C/V)\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ with the sequence topology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] on $\mathcal T_W$ at $\Delta H$: its sheaf topos is $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T_W)/\Delta H$, and restriction is the inverse image of the localization morphism. This identifies that morphism with $\widetilde j$. The ring restricted to $(U,n,s)$ is $B_n(U)$, exactly $C_n(U\to V)$. The same section formula on modules is levelwise $j^{-1}$.

Use the exact equivalences of [lem-pur-sequence-site-completion-projection] for the two coefficient towers. If small skeleta were chosen, use the induced ringed presentation equivalences of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport]; the structural ring identifications are the identities $B_n(U)=C_n(U\to V)$ from step 1. Under these equivalences $\widetilde j^*$ is the levelwise restriction functor $L$. Write $\widetilde J$ for module extension by zero on this slice topos, transported to systems. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] to the same small sequence site and its ring $B_\bullet$ gives an exact additive adjunction $\widetilde J\dashv L$. This application is at the sheaf $\Delta H$, not at an asserted representing object of the sequence site.

Using the supplied normalized coefficient datum, construct levelwise extension, its actual transitions, and morphisms as in original steps 5 and 6. Coefficient naturality, composition and identity give the strict system laws. Transpose levelwise maps using the fixed open adjunction; the unit and counit coherence equations identify exactly the two system-map conditions. This gives J left adjoint to sectionwise restriction L and the level unit/counit normalization. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies it with geometric slice extension, giving additivity and exactness.

lean.statement:
theorem sequenceOpenOrdinary (W : Scheme.{u}) (V : W.ProEt)
    [IsOpenImmersion V.hom]
    (B : ℕ → Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology W) CommRingCat.{max (u + 1) r})
    (τ : ∀ n : ℕ, B (n + 1) ⟶ B n)
    (A : SequenceOpenCoefficientData.{u + 1, u, r} (Scheme.ProEt.topology W) V) :
    ∃ O : SequenceOpenOrdinary.{u + 1, u, r} (Scheme.ProEt.topology W) V B τ,
      O.coefficients = A ∧ O.Transitions
